Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zRndr\zRndr_Draw.cpp
Builds g_zRndr_LensFlareVisibleSampleDefs from queued lens-flare samples starting at startIndex, keeping only enabled samples in the first 0x40 entries whose depth divisor is nonzero.
BN limitation: the loop is anchored on &sample->lensFlareSource, so the decompiler renders sample->depthDivisor as ecx[-2] and the stored sample pointer as &ecx[-4]; the x87 zero compare also remains a status-word temporary.

Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zVideo\zvid_ddd3d.c
BN limitation: quad-batch writes are indexed by g_zVideo_QuadBatchCount << 7, so HLIL keeps raw global-base expressions; they map to one zVideo_QuadBatchItem with TL/BL x=left, TR/BR x=right, top y, bottom y, and one packed ARGB color on all corners.

Original file: GameZRecoil/zVideo/zVideo.cpp. Selects the persisted renderer backend for startup: a nonnegative hwApiIndex commits that accepted hardware API device and returns ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_HARDWARE; -1 binds the software fullscreen dispatch, leaves g_zVideo_pSelectedHwApiDeviceRecord on table entry 0 as a placeholder, clears g_zVideo_pSelectedD3DDeviceInfo, and returns ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_SOFTWARE. BN renders the 4-byte null store to g_zVideo_pSelectedD3DDeviceInfo as memset.

Original file: GameZRecoil/zWeapon/zWeapon.cpp. Processes queued impact callbacks, advances OptCatalog projectile runtime states, updates trail runtime segments, performs raycast hit handling, recycles expired instances, and restores the variant tag/current audio timing state. BN limitation: VC5 x87 trajectory/trail math and large stack raycast buffers leave unimplemented FPU and stack-index artifacts in HLIL; assembly, callees, callback ABI, and applied OptCatalog runtime/trail/raycast types are verified.

Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zWeapon\zWeapon.cpp -- OptCatalog_HandleImpactFromRuntimeProbe.
Processes each raycast hit whose node damage handler is not excluded, computes scaled damage with optional distance falloff, either invokes damage feedback immediately or queues a 64-entry delayed impact record, and returns nonzero when at least one hit was processed.
BN limitation: the enum flag tests still render as high-byte slices because assembly tests AH for OPT_ENTRY_MINE/OPT_ENTRY_UPDATES_STATUS_METER, and the queued impact-position zVec3 copy remains scalarized through a temporary int32_t* even though both source and destination fields are typed as zVec3.

Original file: GameZRecoil/zVideo/zvid_dd.c. function_edits: Retail 0x4164b9/0x4164c6 uses scratch base 0x4edc78 with 12-byte elements. 0x416574-0x416590 copies element zero after the runtime point count. These accesses do not prove the existing 1024-element allocation extent.
Retail 0x46eb23 loads ECX=20 and 0x46eb45 clears 20 dwords from 0x56179c. This proves the initialization span, not independent source-owner acceptance.

Retail 0x459f72 loads divisor 200; the accesses beginning at 0x459f77 use 4-byte floating-point elements at 0x575a80 with index reduction by IDIV. No source-file or call-contract acceptance is asserted here.
Retail entry rejects sample count >=650. 0x49a85d-0x49a891 writes a 20-byte record at 0x62ea04 + count*20, then increments count at 0x62ea00.
Retail walks 20-byte entries from 0x62ea04 using count at 0x62ea00, then clears that count at 0x49a8f6.

Retail walks 20-byte entries from 0x62ea04. 0x49a956 compares the entry address with 0x62ef04 (base +64*20); 0x49a974 appends the queue-entry address to the pointer list at 0x631cd0. The x87 test at 0x49a969 tests AH bit 0x40, not an ordered greater-than predicate.

Retail clears count 0x631ccc, walks queue records with 20-byte stride, and compares the +16 cursor against 0x62ef14 (base +64*20 +16). 0x49aa07 stores the record base into 0x631cd0. This is evidence for the selected input range, not proof of a larger allocation.
0x4acd00
Retail 0x4acd0d rejects unsigned batch count >=16. 0x4acd1d/0x4acd6c multiplies the index by 128; the record base is 0x63363c.
Retail compares the selection with -1, not with an upper capacity bound. The -1 path stores table base 0x633e44 at 0x633e40 and clears 0x6359f4; the other path calls 0x4a8870.
Retail consumes the queue counted at 0x77896c in reverse order, using 68-byte records at 0x778970. This annotation makes no claim about the other runtime layouts or source-file ownership.
Retail 0x4b0ac3 compares the queued-impact count with 64. The append path uses 68-byte records at 0x778970 and increments 0x77896c.
Retail 0x4a7b45 initializes the selected device-record pointer at 0x633e40 to table base 0x633e44. Original source-file placement is not established by this store.
Retail computes an indexed record address from table base 0x633e44 and stores it at 0x633e40. There is no bounds check here; 0x4a7490 checks only the -1 sentinel, not the upper capacity.

Retail 0x4a940b forms the next record pointer from 0x633e44; 0x4a942f compares the accepted-device count with 4. Record stride is 0x6ec. This annotation does not accept the original source owner or file.
